findings.title: readSequence loops forever or misbehaves on indefinite length
findings.body: readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding, so the `while (length > 0)` loop in readSequence is skipped and an empty list is returned without error. Truncated or malformed input is not rejected clearly. A zero-length element could also make the loop spin without progress. Malformed signatures should throw a clear IOException instead.

findings.title: Dead code: results of the encoder calls are discarded
findings.body: Lines 114-115 create ASN1Encoder instances and write the integers, but the results are discarded. This is leftover code with no effect and should be removed.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns a non-BC KeyStore provider
findings.body: The method returns the provider of the default KeyStore type, which is a JDK provider and not BouncyCastle. Callers such as BouncyIntegration that use the provider name to look up BC algorithms will get a mismatched provider, and the method is misleading. Returning null or throwing would be clearer.

findings.title: Providers with equal order are chosen nondeterministically
findings.body: The previous check that failed on multiple providers is gone. Two providers with the same order, such as default and fips, or default and elytron (all 200), now resolve silently by classpath order. A misconfigured classpath is no longer detected, and only a debug log records which provider was ignored.

findings.title: New abstract method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `order()` is added as an abstract method with no default. Any third-party or test CryptoProvider implementation will no longer compile. A default implementation would be backward compatible.
